current.title: James
current.author: Percival L. Everett
current.blurb: A man lives alone in a house of endless halls and tidal seas, keeping careful notes on the statues and the birds. It is a puzzle, but the pleasure of it is the voice — patient, decent, entirely unbothered by the fact that his world makes no sense. Bring your theories; we will disagree warmly.
questions: Does the House work better as a place or as a metaphor — and does it matter?
Piranesi is kind almost to a fault. Is that innocence, or damage?
Where did the ending leave you: relieved, or a bit bereft?
